sentence: This project measures how much time adults with advanced ovarian or metastatic breast cancer spend on cancer-related activities and how that time affects their well-being.
This project studies how a transcription factor keeps breathing-control neurons in the brainstem working, using mice and mutated versions linked to a breathing disorder.
This project studies how small extracellular vesicles made by wound macrophages form and act on other cells to calm inflammation and help wounds close.
This project makes and maintains genetically modified mice, using transgenic or gene-edited mice, for researchers studying diseases of the skeleton and muscles.
This project studies how a gene makes smooth muscle cells in blood vessel walls multiply and change, and how that leads to vascular disease.
This project tests in mouse models whether drugs that target a cancer pathway, combined with immunotherapy, help the body reject head and neck tumors.
This project uses imaging to follow how neural stem cells move toward brain metastases of breast cancer in animal models.
This project combines physics-based thinking with biology to tackle multiscale problems in the life sciences and medicine.
This project studies the neurobiology of drugs of abuse using genetics, neuroscience, neuroimaging, neuropharmacology and large datasets.
This project studies how memory T cells in the lung respond to repeated exposure to house dust mite allergen, a common cause of allergic asthma.
This project tries to find out why bone derived from the neural crest heals faster than other bone, focusing on cells with a neurotrophin receptor.
This project studies the structure and biology of cementum, the bone-like tissue that holds a tooth in place, and how age and disease change it.
This project uses eye tracking and machine learning to build a severity score for children with cortical visual impairment.
This project studies how the molecular signaling behind thyroid eye disease is controlled, focusing on proteins found on the surface of cells.
This project studies the structure and workings of a glycosyltransferase complex in pediatric gliomas driven by a gene fusion.
This project tries to find out how local circuits in the hippocampus control the rapid formation of lasting neuronal representations that support memory.
This project tests whether drugs that block a protein called beta-catenin limit excess cell growth in blood vessel walls, using cultured cells and mouse models.
This project uses quantitative scoring and machine learning to analyze kidney biopsy images and improve how lupus nephritis is judged.
This project lays the groundwork for a treatment for hypoxic brain injury in infants, based on a compound that blocks a plasma membrane protein.
This project tries to find plasma protein biomarkers that can estimate when a stroke began and tell ischemic stroke apart from stroke mimics.
